How should one behave toward a teacher? How should one behave toward elder and more senior bhikṣuṇīs?
How [should one behave] in a village?
How [should one behave] in the forest?
How in the midst of the Saṃgha?
How should one practice regarding the wearing of the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes?
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [Pe] ...
until the Blessed One said:
"Summon those bhikṣuṇīs."
They were then summoned.
The Blessed One questioned them about all of this in detail, [to which they replied],
"Yes, Blessed One."
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, it is not permissible to ordain one who has fewer than twelve years of standing in the rainy-season retreat.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
"Call together the nuns, Gautamī, as many as there are, until they have become thoroughly purified.
Should any nun who has less than twelve years of seniority give formal admission [to a female novice], it is an offense of expiation (pācattika)."
"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*).
"Less than twelve years" means: less than twelve years of rain-seasons (*udaka-varṣa*), less than twelve full years—that is a nun of less than twelve years.
One who has less than twelve years of rain-seasons but has completed twelve full years is also a nun of less than twelve years.

A nun who is less than twelve years [from her full ordination]—that is, one who has completed more than twelve years but is still short of twelve rainy-season years—is a "nun less than twelve years old.
If she was ordained during the winter and undergoes full ordination in that same twelfth year, she is a "nun less than twelve years old" until the *pravāraṇā* ceremony has been performed.
Once the *pravāraṇā* has been performed, she is no longer a "nun less than twelve years old."
Thus she is ordained in the summer or during the rains;
thus she is ordained during the first invitation ceremony (*purimikā varṣopanāyikā*).
She confers ordination before the invitation ceremony (*pravāraṇā*) has been performed.
She was ordained during the later *varṣopanāyikā* (the later retreat).

She ordains [others] before two *pravāraṇās* have been performed; such a nun is one who has less than twelve years [of standing]. One who has completed twelve years of rainy-season retreats (*udakavarṣa*), even if the calendar year is less than twelve, is a nun who has completed twelve years.

A bhikṣuṇī who has completed twelve years of wet-season rains and twelve full years [since ordination] is a bhikṣuṇī of twelve years. A bhikṣuṇī who has completed twelve years of wet-season rains and more than twelve full years [since ordination] is a bhikṣuṇī of twelve years.
One who was ordained in the winter and is ordained again in that twelfth year, after the *pravāraṇā* ceremony has been performed, is a bhikṣuṇī of twelve years.
In this way, she is ordained during the summer or the rainy season.

Likewise, having been ordained when the first rains-retreat (*purimikā varṣopanāyikā*) has been completed and the invitation ceremony (*pravāraṇā*) performed, a nun who has twelve full years of seniority may grant ordination.

Having been ordained during the later rains-retreat (*paścimikā varṣopanāyikā*), she may grant ordination with that twelfth year after two invitation ceremonies have been performed; such a nun has twelve full years of seniority.
If one should ordain [a girl] who is less than twelve years old, it is a *pācattika* offense.
If that nun ordains one who is less than twelve years old, it is a *pācattika* offense; if she causes her to go forth, she incurs an offense of transgressing the discipline (*vinayātikrama*).
A monk also, if he ordains one who is less than twelve years old, incurs an offense of transgressing the discipline.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a nun who has fewer than twelve years [of seniority] should ordain [a candidate], it is an offense of expiation (pācattika)."
Pācattika-dharma 93:
Not endowed with the [necessary] limbs.
207. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
The Blessed One has prescribed a training rule:
it is not permissible to ordain one who is less than twelve years old.
At that time, on that occasion, the group-of-six nuns were exactly twelve years old.
Now they were ordaining and initiating them,
yet they neither admonished nor instructed them.
[The] passage [is] as follows: up to, "How should one practice regarding the wearing of the outer robe (saṃghāṭī) and the carrying of the bowl?
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [The] passage [is] as follows.
When she had been summoned, the Blessed One questioned her about all of that in detail, until she replied,
"Yes, Blessed One."
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, it is not permissible to ordain one who is not endowed with the requisite limbs.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
[This continues] until they become completely purified.
Even if she has completed twelve years and is otherwise qualified, if she should ordain one who lacks the [required] limbs, it is a *pācattika*.
"Having completed twelve years" is as explained in the first training rule (*śikṣāpada*).

And she is "not endowed with the factors" (an-aṅgopetā); "endowed with the factors" (aṅgopetā) means one for whom ten factors are present, as follows: [1] she is restrained by the restraint of the Prātimokṣa; ... [and so on through the ten factors].
She becomes one who is well-versed in the Abhidharma. || 2 ||
She becomes one who is learned in the Vinaya. || 3 ||
She is capable of establishing [others] in the training of higher ethical discipline. || 4 ||
She becomes capable of establishing [others] in the training of higher mind. || 5 ||
She becomes capable of establishing [others] in the training of higher wisdom. || 6 ||
She is capable of restoring herself from an offense she has committed, or of causing another to be restored from one. || 7 ||
She is capable, in times of misfortune, of either withdrawing herself or causing [the husband] to withdraw. 8.
She is capable of attending to the sick herself or of having them attended to.
She is twelve years of age, or more than twelve years of age. ||ḻṃ ||
She in whom these ten factors are found is said to be "endowed with the factors.
By the opposite, she is "not endowed with the factors.
If one who is not endowed with the factors should ordain [a woman], it is a *pācattika* offense.
[The] passage [is] as before, up to the formal rule (*prajñapti*).
If she ordains one who is not endowed with the requisite limbs, she incurs an offense of transgression against the discipline (*vinayātikrama*).

If one ordains [by formal act], it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). If a monk who is not endowed with the requisite limbs ordains or confers full ordination, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
Even if she has completed twelve years [of training], if she is not endowed with the [required] qualities, yet she ordains [a pupil], it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||3||
Pācattika-dharma 94:
On being unappointed. 208. The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
The Blessed One has prescribed a training rule:
"One who is twelve years old and endowed with the [necessary] qualities should be ordained.
Now, those nuns who are twelve years old and endowed with the qualities are ordaining others.
Now the nuns were complaining:
"She has twelve years [of seniority], yet it is not known whether she is endowed with the [necessary] qualities or not."
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī,
and so on until the Blessed One said:
"She must request authorization for ordination."
The formal act (karma) must be performed by means of a ritual motion (karmakārikā).
Let the noble Saṃgha hear me:
if it is the proper time for the Saṃgha, this nun named so-and-so is twelve years of age and endowed with the [required] qualities.

She should request the authorization for ordination from the Saṃgha. The noble lady, the bhikṣuṇī named so-and-so, who is twelve years of age and endowed with the [necessary] qualities, will request the authorization for ordination from the Saṃgha. It is pleasing to the Saṃgha; since there is silence, I shall hold it to be thus.
Now she should make this request:
"I pay homage to the noble Saṃgha.
I, the bhikṣuṇī named so-and-so, am twelve years of age and endowed with the [required] qualities."
I, [name], request the Saṃgha for authorization to provide nursing care.
It would be well, indeed, if the noble Saṃgha would grant me authorization to provide nursing care.
In this manner, the monk should make his request.
The motion: Let the noble Saṃgha hear me.
This bhikṣuṇī, named so-and-so, is twelve years of seniority and endowed with the requisite qualities.
She requests from the Saṃgha the authorization for ordination.

If it is the right time for the Saṃgha, let the Saṃgha grant the authorization for ordination to the nun named so-and-so, who has twelve years of seniority and is endowed with the requisite qualities. This is the formal motion.
Let the noble Saṃgha listen to me.
This nun, named so-and-so, is twelve years of age and endowed with the required qualifications.
She requests formal authorization from the Saṃgha for the ordination of others.
The Saṃgha grants this authorization for the ordination of others to this nun, named so-and-so, who is twelve years of age and endowed with the required qualifications.

Whichever noble ladies approve of the granting by the Saṃgha of the authorization for ordination to the nun named so-and-so, who has twelve years of seniority and is endowed with the [necessary] qualities, let her remain silent. She to whom it does not please should speak.
This is the first formal motion;
likewise the second and the third formal motion.
The Saṃgha has granted the authorization for ordination to the venerable sister named so-and-so, who is twelve years of age and endowed with the requisite qualities.

It is pleasing to the Saṃgha because it is silent; thus do I hold it. Now, indeed, until they have become thoroughly purified—even if she has twelve full years [of seniority] and is endowed with the [required] qualities—if she should ordain one who has not been authorized, there is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
"Endowed with the [required] factors" means that a bhikṣuṇī becomes endowed with the factors by means of ten factors;
the rest is as before.
"Unauthorized" means that she is indeed unauthorized if she has not been authorized.

If she is not endowed with the requisite qualifications and is not formally authorized, and they perform that ritual for her—being defective in the motion (*jñapti*), defective in the assembly (*gaṇa*), or defective in the proclamation (*anuśrāvaṇā*), and corrupted by one or another of the secondary defects of the ritual—then she is thus unauthorized. "Should ordain her" means "should confer full admission (*upasampadā*"); [if she does so, it is] an offense of expiation (*pācattika*).
If that nun ordains one who has not been formally authorized, it is a *pācattika* offense;
if she causes her to go forth, she incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If she is twelve years old and possesses the [required] limbs, yet she ordains her without having been formally authorized, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||4||
Pācattika-dharma 95: Regarding those of bad character, 209. The Blessed One was staying at Vaiśālī.
That nun Kālī, the daughter of a Licchavi who had been ordained within the three-year interval,
has completed her training;
yet she opens the other monasteries with master-keys and duplicate keys and stays there together with householders and wandering mendicants.
She was ordained by her;
now the nuns are complaining:
"Why has she been ordained—this woman of immoral conduct, who picks locks and keeps men as companions?"
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [She said: "Go and summon Kālī.
She was then summoned.
The Blessed One questioned her in detail until she replied, “Yes, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said,
“It is a transgression for you, Kālī.”
"Kālī, this is not the Dharma so long as you continue to ordain one who is immoral, a thief through housebreaking, and a companion to men.
Therefore, it is not permissible, knowing her to be so, to ordain one who is immoral, a thief through housebreaking, and a companion to men.
Now, indeed, the Blessed One [spoke] until they became completely purified."
If a nun, knowing that a woman is immoral, has bolted her door, and keeps company with men, should ordain her, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
"If a nun" means one who is fully ordained (upasampannā).
"Knowing" means she should know it herself or hear it from another.

"Of bad character" means one who has failed in morality or has transgressed the precepts. "A pickpocket" means one who opens the doors of monasteries belonging to others by means of false keys or master-keys.
"One who has a male companion" means...

She dwells in close association with householders and wandering mendicants. "Should she ordain" means: should she confer full admission (*upasampadā*), it is an offense of expiation (*pācattika*), as far as the formal rule (*prajñapti*) is concerned. Now, regarding her who dwells in close association with householders and wandering mendicants: it is not permissible to ordain her. However, if she is now able to fulfill the holy life (*brahmacarya*), she may be ordained after having been separated from that association.

If a monk, knowing that a novice (śrāmaṇera) is of immoral conduct and is in close association with women, should ordain him without having him removed, he incurs an offense of transgressing the Vinaya.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a nun, knowing that a woman is of immoral conduct, keeps her as a door-to-door beggar (prati-tālakinī) with a male companion, it is a pācattika. (5)
Pācattika-dharma 96:
A girl less than twenty years of age. 210. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.

Now, the nuns were ordaining girls who were only ten or twelve years old. These [ordinands] acted without discernment and were not perfected in proper conduct; they did not know how to behave toward their preceptor, nor how to behave regarding the wearing of the outer robe, the bowl, and the monastic robes.
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. ... [the Buddha] said: "Call those bhikṣuṇīs here."
They were then summoned.
The Blessed One questioned them about all of that in detail, until they replied, "Yes, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:

Therefore, it is not permissible to ordain a maiden who is less than twenty years of age. Indeed, the Blessed One has declared that [the rules] shall remain until they are completely purified. Furthermore, whichever nun should ordain a maiden who is less than twenty years of age commits a *pācattika* offense.
"Less than twenty years old" means: less than twenty years of water, less than twenty years of the year—this is "less than twenty years old.

Less than twenty years of water, exactly twenty years of the year—this is "less than twenty years old. Less than twenty years of water, more than twenty years of the year—this is "less than twenty years old."
If she was born in the winter, and one ordains her by means of that twentieth [year] before the *pravāraṇā* has been performed, she is less than twenty years of age.
Likewise if she was born in the summer.
Likewise if she was born during the first *varṣopanāyikā*, and one ordains her by means of that twentieth [year], she is less than twenty years of age.
She was born during the later rains-retreat; he ordains her at twenty years of age,
yet she has not performed the two *pravāraṇā* ceremonies and is less than twenty years old.

If all [the nuns], perceiving her as less than twenty years of age, confer full ordination upon this maiden who is actually less than twenty years of age, they all incur an offense of expiation (pācattika),
and she is not fully ordained.

If one nun perceives her as less than twenty years of age while another nun perceives her as having reached the full age, and they together confer full ordination upon this maiden who is actually less than twenty years of age—
Those who confer full ordination while perceiving [the candidate] as deficient incur an offense of expiation (*pācattika*). There is no offense for those who perceive [her] as complete.
And she is not fully ordained.
If all [the preceptors] ordain one who is less than twenty years of age while perceiving her to be less than twenty years of age, there is no offense for any of them;
and she is properly ordained.

If all [the preceptors] ordain one who is full twenty years of age while perceiving her to be less than twenty years of age, they all incur an offense of transgression against the discipline (*vinayātikrama*).
And she was fully ordained.
One [nun] who was twenty years of age, while perceiving herself as less than twenty years of age, and others who perceived her as being twenty years of age, conferred full ordination upon her.
Those who perceived her as less than twenty years of age committed an offense against the Vinaya.
Furthermore, for those who perceive her as being twenty years of age, there is no offense;
and she is considered fully ordained.
If they ordain all those who are actually twenty years of age while perceiving them all as being so, there is no offense for any of them;
she too is properly ordained.
"A maiden" means a maiden whose celibacy (*brahmacarya*) has not been violated.
"To ordain" means: she should be fully admitted [into the order]; this is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ... [as before] ... up to the formal rule:
"Whosoever among those who have become maidens desires full admission into the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, she should now be granted favor."
When were you born?
If he does not know, the birth register should be examined.
If there is no birth register, the parents should be questioned.
Now, if they do not know either, they should be asked:
"In which kingdom were you born? Or how old were you at that time?"
Whether it be a correct view or a false view,
one must inquire;
one should not proceed according to the influence of someone who is arrogant or someone who is merely eloquent.
Furthermore, the hands and feet must be examined.
Regarding this, the Blessed One said: "If a nun should ordain a maiden who is less than twenty years of age, it is a *pācattika* offense. (6)
Pācattika-dharma 97:
Not having been instructed in the training.
211. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now a training rule has been prescribed by the Blessed One:
"It is not permissible to ordain a maiden who is less than twenty years of age.
Yet those nuns now ordain maidens who are twenty years of age [but have not been instructed in the training].
Now the bhikṣuṇīs were complaining:
"Who knows whether she is twenty years old or not?
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
[The] intermediate passage [is as follows]:
... until the Blessed One said:
"Whichever girl desires this..."

In the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, one should seek full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) into the state of a bhikṣuṇī. That candidate must request from the Saṅgha permission for the instruction in the training for two years. The officiant shall then perform the formal act (*karma*).
Let the noble Saṃgha listen.
This girl named so-and-so, who is eighteen years of age, desires the full ordination and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
If it is the right time for the Saṃgha, let this girl named so-and-so request from the Saṃgha the authorization to undergo the training for two years.
The noble ladies shall request from the Saṅgha the formal authorization for the instruction of two years for an eighteen-year-old maiden.
Since the Saṅgha consents by its silence, I thus hold it to be so. She must now make this request.
I pay homage to the noble Saṅgha.
I, [name], an eighteen-year-old maiden, desire the full ordination and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
Therefore, I request permission for the instruction in the training for two years.
"It would be well indeed if the noble Saṃgha would grant me the formal authorization for the training rules for two years. Thus it should be requested three times.
The formal act (*karma*): "May the noble Saṃgha listen to me."
This maiden named so-and-so, being eighteen years of age, desires the full ordination and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
She requests from the Saṃgha permission for the instruction in training for two years.
If it is the right time for the Saṃgha, let the Saṃgha grant permission for the instruction in training for two years to this maiden named so-and-so, who is eighteen years of age.
This is the formal motion.
Let the noble Saṃgha listen to me:
this maiden named so-and-so, who is eighteen years of age, desires the full ordination and the status of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
She requests from the Saṃgha the authorization for the instruction in the training for two years.
The Saṃgha grants the authorization for the instruction in the training for two years to this maiden of eighteen years named so-and-so.

Whichever noble ladies approve of the granting by the Saṃgha of the authorization for the instruction in the training for two years to this maiden of eighteen years named so-and-so, [let them remain silent].
She who approves of this should remain silent;
she who does not approve should speak.
This is the first formal proclamation (*karmavācanā*).
In this same way, the second and third formal announcements (karma-vācanā) are made.
"Venerable ladies, the Sangha has granted the authorization for the instruction in training for two years to the maiden named so-and-so, who is eighteen years old.
Since there is silence, the Sangha approves of this; thus do I understand it."
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
"Gautamī, assemble the bhikṣuṇīs until they are all present;
even one who has been a maiden for twenty full years."
And if she should ordain one who has not been instructed in the training, it is a *pācattika*.
"Full twenty years" means full twenty years of rainy-season retreats;
it means a full twenty-year cycle.
A full twenty years;
a girl who has completed twenty years; "one who has remained a maiden" means one whose celibacy (*brahmacarya*) has not been violated.
"Unprescribed instruction" means that very instruction which has not been prescribed is "unprescribed instruction.

And they perform that ritual action (karman) in a manner defective in the motion (jñapti), defective in the assembly (gaṇa), and defective in the proclamation (anuśrāvaṇā), being defiled by one or another of the corruptions of the ritual action.
Even so, this is "unprescribed instruction."
"Should ordain" means: should confer full admission; it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
This is the formal rule.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
And even if she has completed twenty years and is a maiden, if one should ordain her without having had her instructed in the training, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||7||
Pācattika-dharma 98: Incomplete Training 212. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now, the nuns were reinstating those who had completed their training;
the nuns then complained:
"This training has been completed, yet it is not recognized."
"Is her training complete or not?
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī,
and so on until the Blessed One said:
"Therefore, it is not permissible to admit one who, although she has been instructed in the training, has not fulfilled the training.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
"Until they have become completely purified..."
If she has already undergone the instruction and is a maiden, and one should ordain her while her instruction remains incomplete, it is a *pācattika*.
"Has already undergone the instruction" means that although she has indeed undergone the instruction, she is not endowed with the requisite qualities (*an-aṅgopetā*);
yet they perform the formal act (*karma*) for her despite this.

It is perfected by the motion (*jñapti*), perfected by the assembly (*gaṇa*), and perfected by the proclamation (*anuśrāvaṇā*); it is not defiled by any one of the various secondary defects of formal acts (*karmopakleśa*).
Thus is this training taught.
"Incomplete training" means that for two years the training was not practiced according to the eighteen modes.
By which eighteen [rules] is she a novice among all the bhikṣuṇīs? And so forth, as previously stated regarding the *gurudharma*s.
Furthermore, it is not permissible for her to enter a village for alms alone;
rather, she must enter for alms together with a bhikṣuṇī or a śrāmaṇerī.
It is not permissible for her to travel alone on a journey.

If she commits any one of the eight offenses, the training must be taught to her again. Starting from the nineteenth year, everything [up to that point] must be made to be performed as a *duṣkṛta* offense. She who trains for less than two years has incomplete training.
"Should she cause [her] to be ordained," that is, should she confer full ordination, there is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"And she is one who has been instructed in the training while still being a maiden."
And if she should ordain her while her training is incomplete, it is a pācattika offense. ||8||
Pācattika-dharma 99:
On not being authorized. 213. The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
Now, a training rule has been prescribed by the Blessed One:
"It is not permissible to ordain one whose training is incomplete.
Yet those nuns now ordain a maiden who is twenty years old, who has completed her training, and whose training is complete.
Now the bhikṣuṇīs complained:
"This training has indeed been taught to her, but we do not know whether her training is complete or not."
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī... [as before] ...until the Blessed One said:

Therefore, whichever twenty-year-old maiden who has undergone training and desires the state of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, she should request the Saṅgha for the authorization of ordination.
Let the noble Saṅgha hear me:
this maiden named so-and-so, being twenty years of age and having completed her training, desires full ordination and the state of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, let this woman named so-and-so request from the Saṅgha the formal authorization for probation (*upasthāpanā-sammuti*). The noble Saṅgha will grant the authorization for probation to this woman named so-and-so. If it is pleasing to the Saṅgha, since there is silence, I shall hold it to be thus.
Now she must request thus:
"I pay homage to the noble Saṃgha.

I, so-and-so by name, a maiden of twenty years who has received the training and completed the training, desire the full ordination and the state of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata."
"I, [name], request the Saṅgha for authorization to attend upon [the candidate].
It would be well indeed if the noble Saṅgha would grant me authorization to attend upon [the candidate].
Thus it should be requested a second and a third time.
The motion: Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.

This girl named so-and-so, who is twenty years of age, has been instructed, has completed her training, and desires the full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) and the state of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata; she requests the Saṅgha for permission to be established [as a candidate].
If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant formal authorization for the ordination of the one named [so-and-so]. This is the motion for the formal proposal.
May the noble Saṃgha listen to me.

This maiden named so-and-so, twenty years of age, who has been instructed in the training and has fulfilled the training, desires the full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) into the state of a bhikṣuṇī within the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata; she requests the Saṃgha for the authorization to be ordained.
The Saṃgha grants formal authorization for ordination to her, [the nun] named so-and-so.
Whichever of the noble ladies approves of the granting of formal authorization for ordination by the Saṃgha to this [nun] named so-and-so, who has twenty years of standing,
let her remain silent.
"Whoever does not approve, let her speak.
Thus is the second and third proclamation of the formal act (*karmavācanā*).

The Saṃgha has granted the authorization for the ordination (*upasthāpanā-sammuti*) of the venerable lady named so-and-so, who is twenty years of age, who has been a maiden, who has completed her training, and whose training is fulfilled."
The Saṅgha grants its consent, since it is silent; thus do I understand this.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
"Gautamī, assemble the bhikṣuṇīs, as many as there are, until they have become completely purified."
[1] Even if she has fulfilled her training, if one should ordain her without having obtained formal consent (*asaṃmatā*), it is an offense of expiation (*pācattika*).

"Even if she has fulfilled her training" means that she has been taught the training for two years by means of eighteen rounds. "And if she is without formal consent" means that she is indeed without consent; likewise, one who has not fulfilled her training is also without consent. And if they perform the ritual act for her while it is deficient in its formal designation (*prajñapti*), deficient in the assembly (*gaṇa*), and deficient in the proclamation (*anuśrāvaṇā*)...

If she is defiled by any one or another of the secondary defilements of action, even so she is not ordained. "Should ordain" means: should confer full admission; [if she does so], it is a *pācattika*.
Up to the point of the designation [of the term].
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
"Even if she has reached twenty years of age and has been a maiden, and she has received instruction and completed her training..."
And if she should cause her to be ordained without having obtained permission, it is a *pācattika* offense. ||9||
Pācattika-dharma 100:
One who has been ordained for less than twelve years and has lived as a householder.
214. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now those Śākya maidens, Malla maidens, and Kolīya maidens who had gone forth from the household life were clever of body, high-spirited, and quick to find fault.
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī asked the Blessed One:
"Is it now possible, Blessed One, to ordain a woman who has lived as a householder for less than twenty years?
The Blessed One said, "It is possible."
They ordain girls who are eight or nine years old and have lived as householders;
these [ordinands] remain without analytical discernment,
just like those under twenty years of age.
The Blessed One said: "It is not permissible to ordain a woman who has lived as a householder for less than twelve years.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
"Summon the bhikṣuṇīs, Gautamī, until they are all assembled.

Whatever bhikṣuṇī should ordain a woman who has lived as a householder for less than twelve years, there is an offense of expiation (pācattika). 'A woman who has lived as a householder' means one whose celibacy (brahmacarya) has been violated."
"Should she ordain her," means: should she confer full admission (upasaṃpadā), it is a *pācattika* offense.
This is the formal rule (*prajñapti*).
She who has lived as a householder and desires full admission into the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, and the state of being a *bhikṣuṇī*, must be assisted by her [the teacher].
...and so on, up to: "The hands and feet must be covered.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If a nun, however, should ordain a woman who has lived as a householder for less than twelve years, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||10||
Summary:
[91] In the presence; [92] less than twelve years; [93] not endowed with the requisite factors.
One who has not been formally ordained; one who is immoral; a maiden who is less than twenty years of age; and one who has not been instructed in the training.
[98] One whose training is incomplete;
[99] one who has not been formally authorized; [100] one who is less than twelve years old for the practice of householdership—thus the tenth section is completed.
Pācattika-dharma 101:
Uninstructed Training. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
The Blessed One has prescribed a training rule:
"It is not permissible to ordain a woman who has lived as a householder for less than twelve years.
Yet now, those nuns are ordaining women who have lived as householders for exactly twelve years.
Now the bhikṣuṇīs were complaining:
"Who knows whether she has twelve full years [of seniority] or not?
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. ... [as before] ...
Just as for a girl who has become a novice at eighteen years of age, the formal authorization for the two-year instruction must be requested.
[This is to be recited] in detail.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If she is twelve years old and has lived as a householder, yet she has not been instructed in the training, and one should nevertheless ordain her, it is a *pācattika*. ||1||
Pācattika-dharma 102:
[Regarding] incomplete training, 216. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Sudinnā, the wife of the tax-collector Abhaṭa, went forth into homelessness.
She had been taught the training rules in the morning;
however, while she was still a householder, she had conceived a child.
He too has grown old;
now the nuns are complaining:
"This is merely one who has completed his training."
And this woman is pregnant.
She clears herself, saying:
"Venerable ladies, since I went forth, I do not recall ever having practiced such an act."
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī... [as before] ...until the Blessed One said: "Since she has now gone forth..."
She does not know how to practice this Dharma. Since she has become a householder and has conceived a child,
it is no longer permissible to ordain her who is now in such a state.
Now, if she gives birth while the midwife has already gone out from the house, then she must be attended to [by another].
Now, when she gives birth to a child and that child has become capable of nursing, then she should be attended to.
Furthermore, if her maternal relative or a kinsman says,
"We shall attend to this child," then she may be ordained.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
"It should be done exactly as it was for one who has remained a maiden.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If she instructs householders in the training rules and causes them to undertake the training in an incomplete manner, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||2||
Pācattika-dharma 103:
On being unappointed. 217. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
The Blessed One has prescribed a training rule:
"It is not permissible to ordain a woman who has lived as a householder for less than twelve years.
Now, those nuns were ordaining women who had lived as householders for twelve full years and who had already received instruction.
Then those bhikṣuṇīs complained:
"This training has indeed been taught to her, but we do not know whether she has fulfilled the training or not.
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
[The full passage] as in the case of a maiden, up until: the Blessed One said,
"And she may be one who has fulfilled the training, even while living the life of a householder."
And if she should ordain her without having obtained consent, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||3||
Pācattika-dharma 104:
Not to instruct. The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
Now those nuns, having repeatedly taken them under their care, did not instruct or admonish them.
Consequently, they grew like *indragava* bulls, [ignorant of] how one should practice regarding the wearing of the outer robe (*saṃghāṭī*), the bowl, and the robes. [The rest is as before.]
The Blessed One said:
"It is a transgression, O bhikṣuṇīs, that you, having ordained [a woman], neither instruct nor admonish her.
Therefore, she must be instructed and admonished for two years."
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
“Gautamī, assemble [the nuns] until they have become thoroughly purified.
Should any nun who has been appointed as an attendant fail to instruct and exhort her for two years, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).”
"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*). [The rest is] as before.
"Attendant" means preceptor (*upādhyāyinī*).
"Those who have been established" means those living together with her.
"Two years" means two rains of two years.
"She should not instruct" means [she should not instruct] either in the Abhidharma or in the Abhivinaya.
The Abhidharma consists of nine types of Sūtras. The Abhivinaya refers to the Prātimokṣa in its detailed classification.

"She shall not instruct" means that if she does not practice proper conduct or practices improper conduct, one should neither expel her nor impose a formal punishment; [if one does so], it is a Pācattika offense.
Now, if that attendant becomes difficult to speak with, or is lax, or indulges in luxury, or has no desire for training, she is to be expelled.
A monk who does not exhort or instruct his co-resident incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If a nun who has acted as a preceptor does not speak to or instruct her sponsored student for two years, it is a *pācattika*. ||4||
Pācattika-dharma 105:
Not to attend upon. 219. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now, those nuns who had been ordained went elsewhere;
then their preceptor-nuns complained,
"The Blessed One has prescribed disciplinary action for us."
These are women who have been ordained as Sāmoktikās.
Now, since those who were previously established [as nuns] go elsewhere,
how are these women to be instructed and exhorted by us?
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [Pe-yā-laṃ] ...
up until she was summoned.
They were asked all of that. "Yes, Blessed One," they replied. The Blessed One said:
It is a transgression, O bhikṣuṇīs, that you have been ordained in this manner; go to another [teacher].
Therefore, a female disciple who has been ordained must follow her preceptor for two years.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
"Gautamī, assemble the bhikṣuṇīs, as many as there are, until they have become thoroughly purified.
Whatever bhikṣuṇī has been ordained [as a preceptor] shall not fail to attend upon or follow her attendant for two years; [if she does so], it is a pācattika offense."

"Again, a nun" refers to one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*). "A student" (*upasthāpitā*) refers to a co-resident (*sārdha-vihāriṇī*). "The preceptor" (*upasthāyikā*) refers to the precept-giver (*upādhyāyinī*).
"Two years" means two years.
"Should not attend upon" means she should not perform personal service.
"Should not follow after" means that she does not go by the same path as he goes; [if she does so], it is a *pācattika*.
This applies as far as the formal designation [of the rule].
Now, if that attendant nun is unwilling to train, or is lax, or is given to luxury,
and another nun observes this...
Thinking, "If she sees [me], she might imitate [my behavior] and that would become an obstacle to my holy life," if she goes by another way, there is no offense.
If a nun does not attend upon or follow her attendant, it is an *pācattika*.
A monk also who does not attend upon or follow his preceptor for two years incurs an offense of transgression against the discipline (*vinayātikrama*).
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a nun who has been ordained does not attend upon or follow her preceptor for two years, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||5||
Pācattika-dharma 106,
Anuvarṣa 220. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now those nuns were ordaining [novices] every year;
they then felt remorse, wondering:
"Is it indeed permissible to do this?"
Or is it not obtainable?
[The passage continues] as far as the Blessed One said:
Therefore, it is not permissible to ordain [a female disciple] every year.
Rather, an interval must be established. Should a nun, however, ordain one every year, it is a *pācattika* offense.

"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*). "Every year" means annually. "Should she ordain" means that if she should ordain [a pupil], it is an offense of expiation (*pācattika*).
As far as the designation goes:
if that nun ordains [a pupil] every year, it is a *pācattika* offense.
She should ordain [only] one year [after her own ordination].
In the subsequent year, the *vīci* (probationary period) must be performed.
Now, if a nun has already performed meritorious deeds, she should be given the training for one year and then placed under formal supervision for another year.
Even if a bhikṣuṇī were to ordain [a disciple] every year, there would be no offense.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a bhikṣuṇī should ordain [a disciple] every year, it is a pācattika. (6)
Pācattika-dharma 107: [Regarding] one who is pure on one side. 221. The Blessed One was staying at Rājagṛha.
Now, at that time, there was a nun named Jetā.
Having had her own female disciple ordained by the nuns, she said to the nun Sthūlanandā:
"Noble lady, my disciple is to be ordained; it would be well, noble lady, if you were to seek out a group of noble ladies."
She went and brought the monks of the group-of-six;
she then said,
"I would not grant full ordination by means of these."
Then, on another day, she gathered a group of excellent monks and conferred the full ordination upon them.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī,
and so on until the Blessed One said:
It is a transgression for you, Jeta, that you thus ordain one who has undergone the *parivāsa* penance while she is still pure in one respect;
that you thus disregard the community. Therefore, it is not permissible to disregard the community.
[The full passage] as before,
until the Blessed One said:
"If a nun should ordain one who has undergone the *parivāsa* penance while being pure on only one side, it is a *pācattika* offense."

"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*). "Pure on one side" means one who has been ordained by a community of nuns. "One who is undergoing probation" means one who has spent the required nights of probation (*parivāsa*).

"One should ordain" means one should grant full admission; it is not a *pārājika* offense for the community of monks, according to the formal rule (*prajñapti*). It is not permissible to ordain a woman who is undergoing probation (*pārivāsikinī*) alone.
Nor is it permissible to confer full ordination (*upasaṃpadā*) with one who is not pure.
Rather, first of all, a group of excellent monks must be assembled.
Now, if some are excellent and others are not excellent, it must be conducted in such a way that the formal acts (*karman*) are of the most excellent kind.
A monk must also perform meritorious deeds.
If he now disregards the community, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
However, if there is fear of an army, fear of a foreign invasion, or a siege of the city, even if he causes a nun on probation (*pārivāsikinī*) to attend to him, there is no offense.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a nun should ordain one who is pure on one side but is a *pārivāsikī*, it is a *pācattika* offense. (7)
Pācattika-dharma 108:
Twenty-two and a half yojanas. The Blessed One was dwelling at Vaiśālī.
That Kālī, the daughter of a Licchavi who had been ordained three years ago,
was now living in close association with householders. She was then addressed by the bhikṣuṇīs:
"Noble Kālī, you know that she who was ordained by you has been in close association with householders and wandering mendicants;
for what reason do you neither remove her yourself nor cause her to be removed?
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
The Blessed One said: "It is a transgression for you, Kāli. [This shall continue] until they have become purified.
Furthermore, if a nun who is an attendant [should act] toward one she has attended in such a manner..."
If she should herself remove [the robe] from the feet, or cause it to be removed—even if only for a distance of six or five *yojanas*—it is a *pācattika*.
"A nun" (*bhikṣuṇī*) means one who has received full ordination (*upasampannā*).
"Attendant" (*upasthāyikā*) means the preceptor (*upādhyāyinī*).
"Attended" means a co-resident nun.
"In such circumstances of misfortune" means that she herself wishes to run back [to her family],
or her relatives wish to have her run back, or she has become associated with others.
"He does not cause it to be removed" means he does not remove it himself, nor does he have others remove it.
"At least six or five yojanas" means that now, six or five is the maximum;
[if it exceeds] six, it is a *pācattika* offense.
This is the formal designation.

Now, if a nun has a co-resident or a pupil who is overly familiar with her, she should be separated from them, or she should be caused to be separated; or else, the praise of wandering on pilgrimage should be spoken to her.
However, if she is now frail due to old age or frail due to illness, she should be caused to be separated by other nuns.
It should be said:
"There will be a salutation to the caitya;
there will be a meeting with the monks."
"When we were young women, we wandered about in this manner.
If a monk does not remove a companion who is longing for such things, nor causes him to be removed, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If a nun who is an attendant does not remove, nor cause to be removed, her dependent from such circumstances of danger—even by as little as five or six *yojanas*—it is a *pācattika*.
This is the 109th *pācattika*-dharma.
How much more so [if she fails to do so when closer]?
223. The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
A nun named Sthūlanandā, being herself not endowed with the requisite qualities, gave formal admission to others;
yet she neither instructed nor exhorted them.
They grow like Indra-cows; they grow like auspicious goats. [The passage continues] as far as: how one should practice regarding the wearing of the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes.
Then that nun was addressed by the other nuns: "But what is the use of ordaining one who is not endowed with the [necessary] limbs? Why does the Noble One speak thus and instruct her? She then said:
"Why, O virtuous ladies, do you look upon my assembly with such envy?"
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
... [The matter was conveyed] until the Blessed One said:
"It is a transgression (duṣkṛta), Nanda; it is not right for you to fall into such a state of reproach."
"Therefore, it is not permissible to engage in the practice of reproaching.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī:
'Gautamī, assemble [the nuns].'"
Until they have become completely purified.
Furthermore, if a nun, being addressed thus by the nuns, should say:
"But what does it matter that she was ordained by a noble lady who lacks the requisite qualifications?"
If a nun, having been told by others, "You should speak thus and be instructed thus," should fall into the state of reproaching them, it is a *pācattika* offense.
"A nun" means one who has received full ordination. "By nuns" means by the Saṃgha, by a group of many, or by a single individual.
Furthermore, regarding "an Āryā who is not endowed with the factors": one who is endowed with the factors is one who possesses ten factors.
She is restrained by the restraint of the Prātimokṣa [1];
she is learned in the Abhidharma [2].
She is well-versed in the Vinaya; [3] ...
up to ... she has reached twelve years of age. [10]

She in whom these ten factors are not found is one who is "not endowed with the factors. If she should voice a complaint, saying, "I shall fall into the state of reproach," it is a *pācattika* offense, as far as the formal rule (*prajñapti*) is concerned.
If that nun, being exhorted by the nuns, should voice a complaint, saying, "Why has an Arya who is not endowed with the factors been ordained? it is a *pācattika* offense.

If a monk, when being addressed by other monks, should fall into the state of reproach, saying, "What is the use of attending upon this venerable one who lacks the requisite qualities? he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore the Blessed One said:

"If a nun, being thus addressed by nuns, should say, 'What is the use of attending upon this noble lady who lacks the requisite qualities? and thereby falls into the state of reproach, it is a *pācattika* offense. (9)
Pācattika-dharma 110:
One should not dismiss [the assembly].
224. The Blessed One was dwelling at Vaiśālī.
Then another *śikṣamāṇā* said to Sthūlanandā:
"Venerable Nandā, please grant me full ordination.
She replied:
"Certainly, I will ordain you," she said;
but she felt embarrassed,
neither ordaining her nor releasing her.
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [The usual formula applies]... up to: "Summon Nandā."
She was then summoned. She was questioned on all of those very points, to which she replied,
“Yes, Blessed One.”
The Blessed One said:
"It is a transgression, Nanda.
Furthermore, whichever nun should speak thus to a *śikṣamāṇā*:"

"If you become one who has completed the preliminary training (*pūra-śikṣā*), then I will ordain you"—having said this, if she neither confers the full ordination nor dismisses her, it is an offense of expiation (*pācattika*). "A nun" means one who is fully ordained;
[the rest is as before].
"A trainee" (śikṣamāṇā) is one who has practiced the training for two years according to the eighteen rules.
"She should speak thus" means as the nun Sthūlanandā did. "I will ordain you"—thus she should be ordained.
Now, if she is not capable herself, another should be requested.
But if she neither attends to him herself, nor requests another, nor dismisses him, saying, "Go wherever you wish; receive full ordination there," [she incurs an offense].
If that nun, having said to a *śikṣamāṇā*, "I will have you ordained," subsequently neither ordains her nor releases her from her commitment, it is a *pācattika* offense. 10.
Pācattika-dharma 111, Vehicle 225. The Blessed One was staying at Vaiśālī.
Then Bhadrā Kāpileyī, having mounted a carriage drawn by four horses, was going to her kinsmen' family. People then complained: "Look, sirs! This female ascetic has great desire!"
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
[This should be repeated] until they have become thoroughly purified.
"Whatever nun should mount a vehicle, that is a *pācattika* offense."
This is the origin of the matter:
the Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
At that time, those daughters of the Śākyas, the Koliyas, and the Licchavis—who were naturally delicate—had gone forth into the religious life.
Walking on foot, they became exhausted.
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, and so forth,
until the Blessed One said:
"Therefore, I authorize [the use of a vehicle] for one who is ill.
Then the Blessed One addressed Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, saying:
"If a nun who is not ill should mount a vehicle, it is a *pācattika* offense."

"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*). "Not ill" is a term withdrawn by the Blessed One; there is no offense for one who is ill. "Illness" means being weak from old age, or weak from disease, or naturally delicate such that she is unable to come on foot—this is the illness intended here.

Regarding vehicles: they are the elephant-vehicle, the horse-vehicle, the camel-vehicle, the ox-vehicle, the donkey-vehicle, the boat-vehicle, the palanquin-vehicle, and the wheeled carriage as the eighth.
If she should mount one, it is a *pācattika* offense.
It is not permissible for a bhikṣuṇī to mount a vehicle.
Where camels or oxen are yoked,
one should instead mount a woman's vehicle;
where female camels or female oxen are yoked, there one should mount.
Now, if she is unconscious and does not perceive whether it is a woman or a man, there is no offense.
Furthermore, if she crosses from one bank to the other by boat, there is no offense.
Or, if the boat is going upstream or downstream, she should resolve upon the condition: "May I not die."
If a monk who is not ill mounts a vehicle, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya; there is no offense if he does so for a valid reason. Therefore, the Blessed One said:
Whatever nun, not being ill, should mount a vehicle, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
Pācattika-dharma 112, Chapter 226. The Blessed One was dwelling at Vaiśālī.

Bhadrā Kāpileyī goes to her family home holding an umbrella and wearing fastened sandals. People now complain: "Look, sirs! Even though she has gone forth as a female ascetic, she still has such great desire."
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī,
and so on until the Blessed One said:
"In that case, it is not permissible [to wear] a parasol or sandals."
This is the origin of the matter:
The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
At that time, those Śākya maidens who had gone forth as nuns were being scorched by the heat as they were walking along.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī... [as before] ... until the Blessed One said: "Therefore, I allow it for one who is ill. [As before.]
Whatever nun, not being ill, should wear a sunshade and sandals, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
"Whatever nun" means one who is fully ordained (upasampannā).
"Not being ill" refers to a term withdrawn by the Blessed One; there is no offense for one who is ill.
What, then, is intended here by "illness"? Is it one weakened by old age, or weakened by disease, or naturally delicate?
[Such a person] might be able to go, but would be scorched by the heat.
"Parasols and sandals": a parasol is called a birch-bark parasol, a palm-leaf parasol, a bamboo parasol, a leaf parasol, or a cloth parasol.
"Sandals" refers to those with a single layer of leather or those that are double-layered.
"Should wear" means to use them; [if one does so], it is a *pācattika* offense.
This is the formal designation:
if that nun, being not ill, carries an umbrella but does not carry sandals, she incurs an offense of transgressing the Vinaya;
if she carries sandals but does not carry an umbrella, she incurs an offense of transgressing the Vinaya.
If he carries both [the sunshade and the robe], it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). If he carries neither, there is no offense.

If a monk also carries a sunshade made of cotton-top or the like, or a folding sunshade (saṃpuṭā) that is not open (anirmokā), he incurs an offense of transgression against the discipline (vinayātikrama).
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"Whatever nun, not being ill, should wear a sunshade and sandals, that is a *pācattika* offense.
*Pācattika-dharma* 113.
Monk 227. The Blessed One was staying at Vaiśālī.
Now, Bhadrā Kāpileyī was going to her family home.
Their beds were spread and re-spread with two or three layers of corpse-cloths; they had to ascend by means of a ladder.
When wandering mendicants and parivrājakas, as well as bhikṣuṇīs, entered for alms, they saw this and complained.
"Look, sirs! Even now this female ascetic is so full of desire.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, who said, "Go and summon Bhadrā."
She was then summoned.
The Blessed One questioned her about all of that in detail, to which she replied,
"Yes, Blessed One."
The Blessed One said:
"Is it true that you sit down or lie down upon a couch or a bench that exceeds the prescribed measure?"
Therefore, it is not permitted to sit down or lie down on a couch or a chair that exceeds the prescribed dimensions.
Indeed, [the rule shall remain] until they become thoroughly purified.
Furthermore, if a nun should sit down or lie down on a couch or a chair that exceeds the prescribed dimensions, it is a *pācattika* offense.
"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*).
"Exceeding the proper measure" means more than the measure of eight *aṅgulas* of a Sugata.
"On a couch or a chair" refers to the fourteen types of couches and the fourteen types of chairs.
"Or should sit down" means he should sit.
"Or should lie down" means he should arrange a bed; [this constitutes] a pācittika offense, according to the formal definition.
If this nun sits down once and remains seated for the entire day, she incurs one *pācattika* offense.

If, however, she sits down again and again, there are as many *pācattika* offenses as there are instances of sitting. If she sits or lies down after burying herself in the ground to a depth exceeding the prescribed measure, there is no offense.
If a monk sits or lies down on a bed or a chair that exceeds the prescribed measure, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"Furthermore, if a bhikṣuṇī [uses one] that exceeds..."
If she should sit down or lie down on a bed or a bench that exceeds the proper measure, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||2||
Pācattika-dharma 114:
On a Single Bedspread 228. The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
Now those nuns of the group-of-six made their beds with a single common covering and blanket;
they broke the frames of the couches, tore the slats, and tore the four-cornered mats.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
When they had been summoned, they were questioned;
they replied, "Yes, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
It is a wrongdoing for you, O bhikṣuṇīs, and so forth...
Furthermore, whichever bhikṣuṇī should share a bed with one who uses the same covering and wearing of robes, it is a pācattika offense.
"Whichever bhikṣuṇī" means one who has received full ordination.
"Having a single covering" means having a single bed-covering. "Having a single upper garment" means having a single cloth.
"Bedding" refers to a bed with a leg support, a stool with a leg support, and so forth, up to mats made of reeds and grass.
"Should arrange" means she should do so. This is an offense of expiation (pācattika), as far as the formal rule (prajñapti) is concerned.
It is not permissible for a nun to arrange a shared bed.

Now, indeed, one should lie alone on a couch. On three stools, two people may lie with their feet extended; they should extend their feet in such a way that their knees do not encroach upon one another.
A woman must sleep alone. When [the bed] is arranged crosswise, three people may sleep upon it, each on their own separate mattress, as in the case of a square couch or a bench.
Now, if there is a bedding made of grass and such, it is not permitted to step over too much of it.
Now, it should be arranged evenly and without gaps using separate individual rugs.
If it is cold, one should each make a single layer by using their own respective inner garments as under-linings. If a monk shares a bed, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a nun should arrange a shared bed, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). ||3||
Pācattika-dharma 115:
Departure. 229. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
A nun named Sthūlanandā, having reserved bedding and seats in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha, departed on a journey.
When visiting nuns arrived,
those nuns were to be assigned the bedding and seats belonging to the Saṅgha in that monastery according to seniority.
Then those nuns complained:
"Why does she now set out on a journey, obstructing the bedding and seats belonging to the Saṃgha? One must not depart without having relinquished the bedding and seats."
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [She said: "Have Nandā summoned. She was then summoned.
This very point was questioned [by the Buddha], up until: "Yes, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"It is a transgression for you, Nanda, that you have set out on a journey without having relinquished the bedding and seating belonging to the Saṅgha."
Therefore, it is not permissible for one to set out on a journey without having relinquished the bedding and seating belonging to the Saṅgha.
Indeed, the Blessed One [has laid down this rule] until they have become completely purified.
Furthermore, if a nun sets out on a journey without having relinquished the bedding and seating belonging to the Saṅgha, it is a *pācattika* offense.
“Again, a nun” means one who is fully ordained.
“Beds and seats belonging to the Saṅgha” means a couch, or a chair, or a mattress, or a square stool, or a bolster, or a pillow.
“Without having returned” means without having given them back.
"If she should set out on a journey," meaning if she goes elsewhere, it is a *pācattika* offense, as far as the formal rule (*prajñapti*) is concerned.
It is not permissible for a nun to set out on a journey without having relinquished the communal bedding and seating.
When she is about to depart, she must say: "I relinquish the bedding and seating so that it may be protected."
If one departs without having formally relinquished [the dwelling], one incurs a *pācattika* offense.
Now, if the monastery consists of a single unit and one sets out on a journey without having relinquished it, one incurs an offense of transgressing the Vinaya.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:
If a nun, without having relinquished a bed or seat belonging to the Saṃgha, should set out on a journey, it is a pācattika offense. 10.137.1 ||
Pācattika-dharma 116:
Entering. 230. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now, while Gartodara’s father was bathing in his own monastery,
Gartodara’s mother went to the monastery unannounced;
having entered, she massaged his back.
She looked at him,
and he then said,
"Ah, it is indeed a woman!"
She said:
"The father of Gartodara is not at fault.
What fault is there in this? Now, I bathe him from time to time."
He then said, "Formerly I was a householder; now I am a renunciant.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
"Call Gartodaramātā.
She was then summoned, and [the Buddha] questioned her about all of that in detail.
“Yes, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said, “On another occasion as well, I shall bathe you.”
He then said:
"It is a transgression for you, O mother of Gartodara, that you approach in this manner, knowing [the time], yet without having been informed beforehand or invited.
Thereupon, the Blessed One said: "Therefore, it is not permissible... [and so on].
If a nun, knowing that a monastery contains monks, should approach it without having previously informed them and without being invited, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
"A nun" means one who has received full ordination.
"Containing monks" means at least where there is even a single monk.
"Of the Saṃgha" means: either that which is in the wilderness (*āraṇyaka*) or that which is near a village (*grāmāntika*).
"Previously unannounced" means: not having been informed.
"Uninvited" means not summoned. "Should approach" means should enter,
as did the nun Gartodaramātā.
[The formula for] the *pācattika* offense, and so forth, up to the formal rule:
Now, when these nuns go to a courtyard (*pariveṇa*), they must announce themselves while standing at the gateway cell, saying:
"I pay homage, Noble One; may we enter."
That monk must now inform the other monks so that the monks do not become separated while engaged in work with clay or work with bricks. If they do become separated, [he must inform them].
If they are not free from attachment, it should be said:
"Sisters, please wait for a moment.
Then, having approached those monks, it should be said to them:
Venerable ones, put on your lower robes and clothe yourselves; the bhikṣuṇīs are entering.
One who is unskilled or ignorant of the proper occasion must not say, "Do not enter so hastily!"
Now, it should indeed be said:
"Bhikṣus, you are separated [from the community]; do not enter.
Now, if they enter without having been informed, it is a pācattika offense.
When she inserts one foot, she incurs an offense of transgression against the discipline (*vinayātikrama*). When she inserts the second foot, it is an offense entailing expiation (*pācattika*).
If she withdraws from that very spot, she incurs an offense of transgression against the discipline.

If a monk enters a nunnery without being announced, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya. Therefore, one should stand at the gateway and snap one's fingers. Thus the Blessed One said.
If a nun, knowing that a monastery belongs to the community of monks, should approach it without prior notice and without being invited, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika). 3.
Pācattika-dharma 117:
With Regard to Humans. The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.
Now, some bhikṣuṇīs, while wandering on tour through the Kośala country, arrived at a village dwelling for the night.
Thereupon, another woman whose husband was away from home said to them,
"Prajāpatī, give us shelter."
She then said,
"Noble lady, my husband is away on a journey;
he might return unexpectedly."
Then they said:
"Who indeed will know this, whether he will come or not?
She gave [it] to Dinna.
Now, when those bhikṣuṇīs had departed, that man arrived at an improper time;
having eaten and drunk, he was oppressed by his afflictions and became intimate with his wife.
Then those nuns were awakened by that sound;
those among them who had not yet departed from passion conceived a perception of repulsiveness.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. [Pe.]
Then the Blessed One said,
"Summon those bhikṣuṇīs. They were summoned, and [the Blessed One questioned] them about all of that exactly as it was.
The Blessed One questioned him in detail,
until [the monk replied], "Yes, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
And yet, knowing this to be so, you nevertheless prepare a bed on a seat in close proximity within a family that provides food.
Therefore, it is not permissible.
This is the origin of the matter.
The Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī.

Now, some bhikṣuṇīs, while wandering on tour through the Kośala country, arrived to stay in a certain village settlement. They then searched the entire village but could not find any house that was without men.
Then, having gone out onto the street, a wind and rainstorm arose at night;
they became distressed and miserable.
The nuns reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
Then the Blessed One said:
"In that case, I authorize [the use of it] during times of wind and during times of rain.
This is the origin of the rule."
The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī. While some bhikṣuṇīs were walking along a street, women informed them [of a situation].
They said, "Enter this house; there is danger here for thieves.
The bhikṣuṇīs said, "No."
The Blessed One has prescribed a training rule:
it is not permissible to take up residence in a house where men are present.
There, during the night, they were harassed by rogues; among them, one woman was led astray from her celibate life.
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
... [the report continued] until the Blessed One said:
"In that case, I authorize [this practice] for as long as there is a time of suspicion regarding men."
If a nun, knowing [the situation], should occupy a bed in a family where food is shared and which is not secluded, except at the proper time, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
Herein, this is the proper time: the time of wind, the time of rain, or the time when there is apprehension of men; this is the proper time in this case.
"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*).
"Knowing" means she should know it herself or hear it from another.
"Shared meal" means a man's meal for a woman, and a woman's meal for a man.

"Family" refers to the brahmin family, up to the royal family, or whatever other families there may be. "Clinging closely" (*anu-pakhajja*) means a dwelling place where husband and wife go back and forth. "Arranging a bed" (*śayyāṃ kalpayan*) means he should lie down on his side.
"Except in the case of an emergency"—this is the phrase withdrawn by the Blessed One; there is no offense.
An emergency may be a wind-emergency, a rain-emergency, or an emergency involving suspicion of men.
Among these, a wind-emergency is neither past nor future.
Rather, it is precisely because it is currently raining;
such is the time of rain.
It is called "the time of suspicion regarding men," thinking, "May there not be an obstacle to my celibate life."
Thus,
this person is neither in the past nor in the future;
rather, he exists only in the present.
This is a *pācattika* offense, as far as the formal rule (*prajñapti*) is concerned.
It is not permissible for a nun, knowing it to be a family where food is shared, to arrange her bed in a secluded place.
However, if it is known that this person is faithful and a familiar acquaintance—
Or, even if others are making their beds by encroaching [upon the space], if she makes her bed without encroaching, there is no offense.
Therefore the Blessed One said:
"If a nun, knowing that it is a family where food is shared in common, should make her bed by encroaching upon the space, except at the proper time, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika)."
In this regard, these are the appropriate occasions: the occasion of wind, the occasion of rain, and the occasion of suspicion of men.
These are the occasions here. ||r||
Pācattika-dharma 118:
On the Road, 232. The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī.
Now, the monks who had spent the rainy season retreat at Vaiśālī set out for Śrāvastī to pay homage at the feet of the Blessed One.
The nuns heard that the monks were indeed going to pay homage at the feet of the Blessed One;
they went to their quarters and said:
"I pay homage, Noble One; let us listen, Noble Sirs. They are going to Śrāvastī to pay homage at the feet of the Blessed One. They said, "Yes; what should be done?"
They said,
"We too shall go.
They said.
"A training rule has been prescribed by the Blessed One: it is not permissible for a nun to travel along a road together [with a monk].
They then said:
'When, O noble ladies, will you depart?'"
They said,
"On such-and-such a day.
Then, counting the days one by one and two by two, they thought, "We shall go on that day."
Now, those women, having already finished their meal by nature of things, dressed themselves, put on their robes, took up their bowls and outer garments, and stood on the path.
Those monks set out at that time;
seeing them, they said:
"Venerable ones, those sisters are going very quickly;
those nuns are also going very quickly. Then those monks ran after them.
Those nuns also ran out.
Now, among them, those nuns who were young and strong pursued those monks;
however, those who were there aged and weak, or weakened by illness, or naturally delicate, were left behind and trampled.
The bhikṣuṇīs reported this matter to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, and so on,
until the Blessed One said:
"How can you indeed set out across foreign kingdoms and across foreign countries without a caravan?"
Therefore, it is not permissible for a nun to set out on a journey across a foreign kingdom or across a foreign country without a caravan,
until she has become thoroughly purified [of her offense].
Should any nun set out on a journey across a foreign kingdom or across a foreign country without a caravan, it is a *pācattika* offense.
"Again, a nun" means one who is fully ordained (*upasampannā*).
"Beyond the kingdom" means another kingdom.
"Beyond the district" means another district.
"Without a caravan" means that a caravan—whether a householders' caravan, a renunciant's caravan, or a wagon caravan—must be sought out.
"On a journey" means she departs elsewhere.
It is an offense of expiation (*pācattika*), as far as the formal rule (*prajñapti*) extends.
If this nun sets out on a journey without a caravan,
when the road has been traversed, it is a *pācattika* offense.
But now, if she travels together with a caravan...

Those who set out on level ground but enter uneven ground incur an offense of transgression against the Vinaya. Those who set out on uneven ground but enter level ground incur an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Those who set out on level ground and enter level ground: there is no offense.
If they set out on a dangerous path and enter a dangerous place, they incur a *pācattika* offense.
If a monk also travels along a path that is without a caravan, and which is considered dangerous, fearful, and full of apprehension, he incurs an offense of transgression against the Vinaya.
Therefore, the Blessed One said:

If a nun should set out on a journey across kingdoms or across districts without a caravan, it is an offense of expiation (pācattika).
